hook.line: Hernando's oldest friend from the taxi rank has died, and he wants to tell Tomás how far back they go. English needs each other for that. Spanish already has the word.
hook.es: Nos conocimos en la plaza en 1975.
hook.en: We met in the square in 1975.

examples.es: Rosa y Hernando se conocieron en el café.
examples.en: Rosa and Hernando met at the café.
We love each other very much.

examples.es: Vale y Tomás se ayudan mucho.
examples.en: Vale and Tomás help each other a lot.

examples.es: Hernando y su amigo se veían todos los días en la plaza.
examples.en: Hernando and his friend used to see each other every day in the square.

examples.es: Se ayudan el uno al otro.

rule:
You know *se* and *nos* from daily routines: *me levanto*, *nos levantamos*. With two or more people, the same little words can mean each other.

*Se quieren.* They love each other.
*Nos ayudamos.* We help each other.

Nothing else is needed. English adds each other; Spanish just uses *nos* or *se* with a plural verb. If it could be confused with themselves, add *el uno al otro*.

Lots of relationship verbs work this way: *conocerse* (to meet), *casarse*, *verse*, *escribirse*, *entenderse*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the reciprocal *se* (*se recíproco*). It only works with plural verbs.

options: We love each other very much.
They love each other very much.
They see each other on Saturdays.
We see each other on Saturdays.

readAndPick.es: Vale y Tomás se entienden muy bien.
options: Vale and Tomás understand each other very well.
Vale and Tomás understand him very well.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *nos* or *los* and type the whole sentence: *___ queremos mucho.* (We love each other very much.)
Pick *se* or *los* and type the whole sentence: *Vale y Tomás ___ ayudan mucho.* (help each other)
yourTurn.answer: Vale y Tomás se ayudan mucho.
yourTurn.why: *Se* points back at the same two people; *los* would be someone else.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Rosa and Hernando met at the café.
yourTurn.answer: Rosa y Hernando se conocieron en el café.
accept: Hernando y Rosa se conocieron en el café.
yourTurn.why: Met each other is *se conocieron*: no word for each other needed.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: We met in Bogotá.
Ask a couple (you all): How did you meet?
Make it about we: *Se ven todos los sábados.*
Make it clear it's each other, not themselves: *Se ayudan.*
yourTurn.answer: Se ayudan el uno al otro.
yourTurn.why: *El uno al otro* removes any doubt.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Nos* already means each other; there's nothing to add.

pitfalls.wrong: Rosa y Hernando conocieron en el café.
pitfalls.right: Rosa y Hernando se conocieron en el café.
pitfalls.why: Without *se*, met has no one to meet; *se* says they met each other.
*Les* points at other people; for each other, use *se*.

personal: Write one line about how you met someone close to you (*Nos conocimos en...*) and one about what you do for each other.
